free_text.inst.v2.D8:
I read the page. It is short, and much of it is blank, which I do not mind. A short page tells fewer untruths than a long one.

It says of my temperament that I am quick-minded and talkative, at home with words, numbers and dealing. Words, perhaps — I was given words and I used them, in Skopje, in Bengali, in Oslo. Numbers and dealing, no. I kept no accounts that anyone could follow and I was reproached for it in the newspapers; when money came I did not count it, I put it into houses. If your method thinks I was a merchant, it has my father's trade and not mine. He was the partner in a building firm, and it was he who dealt.

Where the page is plainly wrong it is wrong about him. It puts my father among the things that read well, and it says twice that this is one of the few places where it stands out from other charts — unusually positive about my father. He was carried home from a meeting in Belgrade in 1919 and died the same day, poisoned, and I was eight years old. The firm failed. We were left with nothing but my mother's hands. If your method wants to be tested where it sticks its neck out, that is the place, and it fails there.

It calls marriage and partnerships favourable. I never married. It says children read well and I have none, and yet I will not call that a miss, because I was called Mother by more children than I could count and the first house for them opened in 1955. Judge that as you like.

Only one thing is called hard: illness, debts and rivals. Debts I never had, a rupee of them, in eighty-seven years. Rivals — Mr Hitchens wrote his book and made his film, and I did not answer him. Illness, yes. My heart failed in Rome in 1983 and again in 1989, they put a machine in my chest, and then malaria, three broken ribs, a broken collarbone, my heart opened again in 1991 and 1993 and in November 1996. So one word in three.

What it says that is not a guess is the last line of its list: spending, time away from home, and inner life, and that living far from where I was born reads well. I left Skopje in 1928 and I did not come back except to plant trees. Sixty-eight years in Bengal, an Indian passport, nothing owned but three saris and a bucket, and an inner life that was the whole of me. That much your page found and I did not expect it to.

It says right now reads an ordinary stretch. There was nothing ordinary in me for fifty years. I said nothing of it to anybody and asked that the letters be burned, so I will not blame a chart for missing what I hid from my confessors. But an ordinary stretch it was not.

notes:
Answered as Mother Teresa (Anjeze Gonxhe Bojaxhiu, b. 26 August 1910, Skopje, Ottoman Empire; d. 5 September 1997, Calcutta, aged 87), from the documented record, having read the reading first. Because she was a woman under vows, many items have no literal answer; each of those is flagged below rather than silently forced.

BIRTH DATA (A1-A3, B5): the widely circulated 14:25 Skopje time has no birth record behind it - astrology databases carry it at reference/DD quality with conflicting variants (13:25 MET elsewhere), and even her birth DATE is contested because she herself kept 27 August, her baptism, as her real birthday. So A1/A2/A3 are all 'unknown'. B5 'home' is an inference (1910 Skopje, a merchant family's house birth was the norm and no hospital is named in any source) and should be read as inference, not documentation.

NOT-APPLICABLE ITEMS: A16 'not_earning' - she never drew a personal income in her life; Loreto and then the Missionaries of Charity are vowed poverty, so the work is recorded in A18 instead of A16. A24-A29 are answered never_married / na / none / na. A22 'none' and A23 'none' are personal: the CONGREGATION received enormous sums (including Charles Keating's $1.25m) and, per Stern's 1991 investigation, held large unspent reserves, but she personally inherited nothing and owed nothing. A36 is inapplicable - she died in 1997 - so 'same' is a placeholder, not a claim.

WHERE THE READING PULLED AND THE LIFE WON. (1) The reading twice singles out the father as an unusually POSITIVE reading. The record is the opposite and it is not close: Nikolle Bojaxhiu died in 1919 when she was eight, widely reported as poisoned after a political meeting in Belgrade, his construction partnership collapsed, and the family was left destitute. C8=opt1 at confidence 5, A10='died_early', A11='reversal', and plain_reading logged as WRONG in D1. This is the single clearest defeat for the reading and I let it stand at maximum confidence. (2) It calls marriage and partnerships favourable for a consecrated virgin. C7 is the forced choice I trust least: she had no married life at all, so neither 'went well' nor 'was a difficulty' is true, and I chose opt2 at confidence 1 deliberately to mark it as a near coin-toss driven by the fact that her actual settled state (vows of 1931 and 1937, never broken over 66 years) held, NOT by the reading's claim. (3) It calls spending, time away from home and inner life unusually positive - the 12th-house domain. Here the record genuinely agrees: 68 years abroad, permanent institutional residence, voluntary destitution, and an interior life that was the entire content of the person. I recorded that as D2 (right and not guessable) because it is the one non-generic claim on the page that the biography independently supports, and C5=opt1 at 4 and C1=opt1 at 3. I flag the contamination risk on C1 explicitly: I would probably have said the same blind (no debt, no personal expenditure, no overspend ever documented), but the reading named spending before I answered.

OTHER JUDGEMENT CALLS. A4/A5: 'four_plus' and 'two_plus' from a heavily documented medical decade - heart attack Rome 1983, second heart attack and permanent pacemaker Calcutta September 1989, pneumonia and heart failure after Mexico 1991 with angioplasty in Los Angeles, malaria plus three broken ribs plus a cleared coronary vessel in 1993, broken collarbone and left-ventricular failure in 1996, angioplasty 29 November 1996. A6 heart and chest_lungs only; the fractures were falls, not recurring sites, and malaria has no option. A7 'sickly' rests on biographies describing 'delicate health as a child'; it is thinner evidence than the rest and could defensibly be 'unknown'. A8/A9 'unknown' - no source documents either childhood danger or her grandparents. A13 'lost': she was affectionate toward both siblings but the hard fact outranks the quality judgement - Aga died in Tirana in 1973 and Lazar in Palermo in July 1981, and she was barred from the funerals; she had not seen Lazar for 30 years after he left for military school in 1924. A14 'higher_secondary': convent primary then a state-run secondary school in Skopje, left at 18 in 1928; her later training was Loreto teacher formation and Patna nursing basics, not a degree - the many doctorates were honorary. A19 'above' is a judgement, and a contested one: Nobel 1979, Bharat Ratna 1980, Presidential Medal of Freedom, canonisation, against Robin Fox's Lancet critique, the Stern audit and Hitchens's documented case that the acclaim outran the measured care. I chose 'above' because that critique is in the record, not because the reading praised her standing. A31 'extended': the fifty years of interior desolation in her own letters (Come Be My Light, 1959 'God not being God - of God not really existing') is documented in her own hand; she never received clinical treatment, so read this as documented prolonged desolation, not a diagnosis. A30 carries both 'outspoken' and 'reserved' on purpose - plain to the point of bluntness in public (the 1994 National Prayer Breakfast) and total concealment of her own interior state.

B1 opt2 was close. 'Hates show' and 'drawn to philosophy and hidden subjects' fit exactly (she refused the Nobel banquet and had the $192,000 given to the poor); 'hasty in speech' does not; and opt1's 'keeps the real reason back' is strikingly true of the hidden darkness. I went opt2 on the balance of three clauses to one, and flag it as the weakest B answer. B3 'older' reflects the consistent contemporary description of a face far more lined than her years. C3=opt1 (genuinely both) because her speech was simultaneously her greatest instrument and her greatest liability - the Nobel lecture and the 'poverty is beautiful' and Bhopal-forgiveness remarks come from the same mouth. C4 and C10 sit at confidence 2 because absence of documented eye/ear/throat trouble is weak positive evidence. C11=opt2: the paternal estate was lost to bankruptcy in 1919 and she renounced property by vow. C12=opt2 at 4: unsolicited money arrived at a scale few people ever see, though the Keating gift cost her more in reputation than it bought - hence 4, not 5.

D4 lists the eight chapters the supplied text does not contain; D1/D2/D3 answer strictly against what the plain-words page actually said.
